summary: A fiction excerpt in which Lexy spends a quiet spring afternoon by a stream with Houseman, a frank, cheerful cargo-steamer sailor from Baltimore, and feels they are kindred spirits. Mrs. Royce sees them returning and concludes he is 'the one,' while George Grey, secretly suffering, hides his pain in the sitting room. Lexy then introduces Houseman as Caroline Enderby's fiancé. An out-of-place line mentions Caleb seeing the 'Girl with a Pearl Earring' painting in 2013.
one_line: Lexy spends an idyllic spring afternoon with the blunt sailor Houseman, while Mrs. Royce misreads the romance and George Grey silently suffers.
key_facts: Houseman skipped stones by the stream while Lexy watched minnows in the clear water.
Houseman is from Baltimore; his father and grandfather were both in the navy, but he rejected the navy as 'too cut and dried'.
Houseman now works on a cargo steamer and likes it.
Houseman is twenty-six, has two brothers in the navy and three married sisters, and both parents are living.
Lexy considers Houseman honest, blunt, careless and fearless, a comrade and ally without equal.
Houseman is an authority on oysters, while Lexy, as a New Englander, has opinions on clam chowder.
When they turned homeward at sunset, Houseman's only remark on the poetic hour was that he was hungry; Lexy replied 'So am I!'
Mrs. Royce watched them from the kitchen window, decided 'He's the one!' and began making a chocolate cake.
Mrs. Royce hummed a song about a young man on Springfield Mountain who killed a 'pesky sarpent'.
George Grey sat in the sitting room smoking and pretending to read, never turning a page, while suffering horribly inside.
Lexy introduced Houseman to George as 'Caroline Enderby's fiancé' and said she had told him the whole thing.
An out-of-place sentence states that in 2013 Caleb finally saw the original 'Girl with a Pearl Earring' painting up close after hours in line.
